provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: My school family
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify school helpers.
The pupils should be able to show appreciation to school staff.
Introduction:
We all come to school every day. School has many people who help us.
Content:
School family includes teachers, cleaners, cooks and security men. Teachers teach us. Cleaners sweep our classrooms. Cooks prepare our food. Security men keep us safe. We say thank you to all helpers.
Class activity:
Pupils will draw pictures of their favorite school helper and give it to them.
Evaluation questions:
Who sweeps our classroom?
Who teaches you numbers?
How do we say thank you to the cook?
Summary:
Our school family works together to keep us safe and help us learn.

topics.title: Feelings deep dive
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name different feelings.
The pupils should be able to express feelings with words.
Introduction:
We all feel different things each day. Sometimes we feel happy. Sometimes we feel sad.
Content:
Feelings are inside us. We feel happy when we play. We feel proud when we finish work. We feel jealous when someone has what we want. We can talk about our feelings with words. Say I feel happy when I play.
Class activity:
Pupils will make faces showing different feelings and name them.
Evaluation questions:
What do you feel when you get a new toy?
What feeling word means you want what someone else has?
How can we tell others about our feelings?
Summary:
All feelings are okay. We use words to share how we feel.

topics.title: Conflict steps
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list steps to solve conflicts.
The pupils should be able to practice conflict resolution.
Introduction:
Sometimes friends disagree. We need steps to solve problems.
Content:
When we have a conflict we must first stop and calm down. Then we talk about the problem. Next we listen to the other person. Finally we agree on a solution. For example if two children want the same toy they can take turns.
Class activity:
Pupils will act out scenarios using stop, talk, listen, agree steps.
Evaluation questions:
What is the first step when friends disagree?
What should we do after talking about a problem?
How can we solve a fight over a toy?
Summary:
We use four steps to solve problems with friends.

topics.title: Team projects
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to work in groups.
The pupils should be able to create a group poster.
Introduction:
Working together is fun. We can do big things when we help each other.
Content:
Team projects mean we work together. We share ideas. We help each other. We listen to friends. For example we can make a poster about animals. Some draw. Some color. Some write names.
Class activity:
Pupils will work in groups to create a poster about our school.
Evaluation questions:
What is good about working in a team?
What job can you do on a poster?
How do we help friends in a team?
Summary:
Teamwork helps us make beautiful things together.

topics.title: Responsibility chart
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name school responsibilities.
The pupils should be able to list home duties.
Introduction:
We all have jobs to do at school. We also have jobs at home.
Content:
At school our responsibilities include keeping our desk tidy. We line up quietly. We share toys. At home we sweep the floor. We wash plates. We put away clothes. Doing jobs makes us proud.
Class activity:
Pupils will draw their favorite home and school responsibility on a chart.
Evaluation questions:
What is your job in the classroom?
What chore do you help with at home?
Why is it good to do our responsibilities?
Summary:
Responsibilities help us learn and help our families.

topics.title: Money habits
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain saving money.
The pupils should be able to identify wise spending.
Introduction:
Money is naira notes and coins. We get money from parents.
Content:
Saving means keeping money for later. We can save in a piggy bank. Spending wisely means buying what we need. We need food and books. We want toys and sweets. We should buy needs first. Our class will make a saving jar together.
Class activity:
Pupils will add naira coins to a class saving jar and talk about what to save for.
Evaluation questions:
What is saving money?
What should we buy first needs or wants?
Where do we keep our class savings?
Summary:
Saving helps us get big things we want later.

topics.title: Digital basics
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to ask before using devices.
The pupils should be able to set screen time limits.
Introduction:
Phones and tablets are digital devices. They help us learn and play.
Content:
We must ask before using phones or tablets. We use devices with grown - ups help. Screen time is how long we watch screens. Too much screen time hurts our eyes. Our class will make a screen time agreement.
Class activity:
Pupils will make a chart showing good screen time habits.
Evaluation questions:
What should we say before using a phone?
Why is too much screen time bad?
How can we limit our screen time?
Summary:
Using devices wisely keeps us safe and healthy.

topics.title: Our neighbourhood
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify places in the neighbourhood.
The pupils should be able to draw a simple map.
Introduction:
Our neighbourhood has many important places. We visit them every day.
Content:
Neighbourhood places include houses where we live. Shops where we buy food. Clinics where we get help. Schools where we learn. We can draw a map showing our street and these places.
Class activity:
Pupils will draw a map of their street showing important places.
Evaluation questions:
What places do we have in our neighbourhood?
Where do we buy rice and beans?
What does a doctor do at the clinic?
Summary:
Neighbourhood places help us get what we need.

topics.title: Being inclusive
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to invite others to play.
The pupils should be able to include everyone.
Introduction:
Playing with friends is fun. Everyone should be able to join.
Content:
No one plays alone means we include all friends. We can invite others by saying can you play with us. We include friends by sharing toys and taking turns. Everyone has fun when we play together.
Class activity:
Pupils will practice inviting a classmate who is sitting alone to join their game.
Evaluation questions:
What does no one plays alone mean?
How can we invite someone to play?
Why is it good to include everyone?
Summary:
Including friends makes playtime happy for everyone.

topics.title: Revision and community project
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recall what we learned.
The pupils should be able to present our kindness project.
Introduction:
We learned many things about being good friends and community helpers.
Content:
We remember feelings, conflict steps, teamwork, responsibilities, money, digital devices, neighbourhood and including others. Our class made a kindness project. We will show what we made to the school.
Class activity:
Pupils will present their class kindness project to other classes.
Evaluation questions:
What is one thing we learned about feelings?
How do we solve conflicts with friends?
What is our kindness project about?
Summary:
We shared what we learned and showed our kindness to the school.
